name: David J. Cappelleri
title: Professor of Mechanical Engineering; Assistant Vice President for Research Innovation
department: Mechanical Engineering; Biomedical Engineering by courtesy; West Lafayette
fitReason: A concrete physical-AI match in agricultural manipulation and sensing, with learning used to guide real interventions. The lab spans substantial hardware design as well, so project selection should emphasize perception, grasping or robot-learning software.

physicalEvidence.summary: In his July 1, 2026 Purdue research account, Cappelleri describes current P-AgBot farm testing and P-AgSAMPLE deep-learning leaf detection, pose estimation and grasp planning for physical sampling. The apparatus is a Clearpath Jackal with Kinova Gen3 Lite, RGB/RGB-D and LiDAR sensing, and a custom leaf-cutting end effector. The lab identifies agricultural PhD researchers and his directorship. The 2023 leaf-learning publication is historical method evidence, not relabelled as a 2026 experiment.

shortVisit.summary: The full Prospective Students page discusses Purdue degree admission, PhD research assistantships, thesis master’s support and postdocs. It does not give an explicit external short-visit route. A current People-page entry labels a master’s researcher Visiting Student; this is hosting precedent, not an open invitation or summer 2027 acceptance.

scoreReasons.fit: Concrete learning-guided physical manipulation and field sensing, within a hardware-heavy multi-scale laboratory.
scoreReasons.physical: Detailed PI-authored current university account ties learned sampling, named apparatus and field testing to own lab.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Current visitor precedent alone gives no open-pathway credit; published intake is degree/postdoc focused.
scoreReasons.freshness: Explicit July 2026 research report and current lab research programme.

The lab roster has stale membership entries: Kitae Kim is now an NC State Assistant Professor (2026 new-faculty cohort), not a current Purdue PhD student. The July 2026 PI-authored Purdue apparatus/field evidence remains the basis for own-lab credit; no 2027 staffing assumption is made.

The verified learning is within perception and manipulation planning, not a demonstrated foundation-model end-to-end policy. The university account is a direct PI-authored research report, not a newly audited full technical experiment paper.

No quantitative field success is claimed from the July 2026 report. The 2025 summer abstract book surfaced as an indexed primary excerpt but its PDF retrieval failed, so its numerical results are not used.

Existing Purdue review supports formal visitor and foreign-degree-related Student Intern categories in principle, with personal/family funds possible subject to approval. Visitor research must serve the visitor’s own academic development and cannot be replaced with informal volunteering. Exact category, eight weeks and 2027 costs remain host/ISS decisions.
